question: Which of the following group of organisms obtains nutrition from other plants and organisms without killing them?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lice, Tapeworm, Leech, Dodder**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lice, Tapeworm, Leech, Dodder** are examples of organisms that obtain nutrition from other plants and organisms without killing them.
 
• These organisms are known as **parasites**, and they rely on a host for their nutrients.
 
• Unlike predators, parasites do not typically kill their host but may cause harm or discomfort over time.
 
• Parasites have evolved various mechanisms to attach to and derive nutrients from their hosts.
 
• For example, **lice** feed on the blood of mammals, **tapeworms** live in the intestines of animals, **leeches** attach to the skin and also feed on blood, and **dodder** plants wrap around other plants to extract nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Parasites can be **ectoparasites** (living on the surface of the host) or **endoparasites** (living inside the host).
 
• They often have specialized adaptations to their parasitic lifestyle, such as hooks, suckers, or specialized mouthparts.
 
• While they do not kill their host outright, parasites can significantly impact the host's health by draining nutrients, causing disease, or weakening the host's immune system.
 
• Control and management of parasitic infestations are important in both agriculture and medicine to prevent the negative impacts on plants, animals, and humans.
